I just had a good idea, that I think can help out players a lot.

Pulled Fangs was previously very useful, and as most agreed, too useful.
At first I was happy to see it "fixed" in the last rulings...especially
so, because I was also a fan of Disarm (a balanced PF). Limiting to
potence-vampires seemed like just the right restriction.

However, I also have 40+ Pulled Fangs. :) And, being rare, we can all
attest to the scramble to accumulate those in the past, trading, buying
whenever not sold out, at $2 or more each. An unfortunate case of a
rare being commonly useful. :)

Now I am sure lots of us have a large investment which is marginally
useful, and certainly not in any of the ways we used to use it, or had
planned to use it. Not only is it debatably useful, but you can now
Pull 12 (?) fangs from that pesky IC member... :)

Now as much as I like Disarm, it suffers from the same rarity problem,
only much worse. Sabbat shows no signs of ever being cheap like Jyhad,
Disarm sells for $3+, and I don't think they ever get traded. This is
a shame, since it would fit perfectly in all those potence decks that
packed 6+ Pulled Fangs.

My suggestion, LSJ, is that PF remain aggro, but have errata to require
potence.

It is the same amount of errata, so the confusion could be no worse.
It will actually not be quite as good as Disarm, but would work well
enough. The silliness of pulling out a lot of teeth wouldn't be
possible.

In fact, unless someone here convinces me that my idea is bad, I think
I will try to institute this in our play group. I certainly don't see
that it could possibly unbalance things, compared to Disarm. And god
forbid I would ever have to proxy cards... :)

I'm here to convince you that it is not a good idea. The biggest problem with
Pulled Fangs (pre 7/7) is not that it can be used multiple times (and neither
the 7/7 errata or your suggestion prevent this aplication of the card), but
that if it does aggrivated damage, it is obscenely powerful, and will burn a
vampire every time it is played. Requiring a vampire to have Potence to play
it is a cost of sorts, but as most of the vamps that play PF have Pot anyway,
it isn't much of a hurdle.

The problem is that when PF does aggro damage, it is painfully easy to burn
vampires. You have 4 blood. I Immortally Grapple you, hit you for 5 damage,
and play Pulled Fangs. You are burned. It is just too easy. The difference
between Pulled Fangs and Disarm is that PF burns you while Disarm does not (it
specifically just sends you to torpor). The real comparison is between Pulled
Fangs and Decapitate. Pulled Fangs allows you to burn a vampire already on the
way to torpor, but it costs you no blood and no discipline. Decapitate allows
you to burn a vampire already on the way to torpor, but it costs you 2 blood
and requires superior Potence. The cost of Decapitate justifies its ability.
The cost of Pulled Fangs (even if it requires Potence) simply does not.

When Pulled Fangs is played in a Potence deck, and it does aggro damage, it
will burn a vampire every time it is played. Very simple.

However, if Pulled Fangs had its wording changed to the same template as Disarm
(sends to torpor, rather than does aggro damage), this would not be a problem,
but it would still be too powerful. I suspect that in the end, PF not doing
aggro damage is the easiest and most appropriate fix.

"The silliness of pulling out a lot of teeth wouldn't be
possible."

I don't see how this changes. The card has nothing on it to prevent multiples
from being played, there is no eratta to prevent multiples from being played,
and your proposed fix has nothing in it to prevent multiples from being played.
Please explain.

Ok, I'm not exactly one in favour for changing rules, but since this is
an arguable interpretation of the card text (and I don't have to use it
anyway, just thought I'd throw it in), how about this.

Pulled fangs is a combat card (no arguments there) and is only usable if
your minion does more damage at close range than the opposing minion,
therefore can only be used after damage resolution (again no arguments).
Now in no other case can a combat card be used after combat ends (apart
from cards like psyche, which explicitly state 'use after combat ends',
or Amaranth 'use when a vampire goes to torpor'). Therefore wouldn't it
be reasonable to assume that pulled fangs could not be used after combat
ends.

This would not only eliminate the playing of multiple PF, but since
combat ends immediately when a vampire goes to torpor, this would also
make it impossible to burn a vampire with PF (You couldn't play it on a
vamp already going to torpor, the aggro damage would only be able to
send them to torpor - no more).

Anyway, that about covers it. Can anyone see any problems with that? It
isn't actually changing any of the rules at all - just changing the way
that we interpret a card (which makes much more sense to me then
changing everything... But we won't start that again ;-)

Martin.

**** Note to those just joining the thread: ***
This discussion is about the way Pulled Fangs used to work (back
when the damage it dealt was aggravated).

Since PF no longer does aggravated damage (Rule Team Rulings of
7 July 1998), the question is not as interesting now.
************************************************

That ruling [allowing multiple PF] came in the Rules Team Rulings
of 6 September 1995.

PF itself (actual card text) has no explicit restriction at all
on when it can be played. This includes the V:TES version of the
card, which was printed well after the "during the press step"
ruling (see below). But it does have an implicit restriction:
you have to know that you deal more damage than your opponent.
You only know this for certain after all strikes that are going
to be resolved have been resolved.

The explicit restriction (at the end of a round) was added to
clarify the original intent of the card, since some players
were questioning whether PF could be played before additional
strikes resolved.

The original form of that restriction was issued by the Rules Team
in the Rulings Summary of 9 November 1994. In that statement,
however, the RT used the phrase "during the press step", which
inadvertently prohibited PF from being played if the victim was
going to torpor (from too much damage, or from agg damage, or
whatever). This restriction was not part of the intended use, as
witnessed by the "not usable by a dying ally or a vampire going
into torpor" clause (which would have no effect if PF was only
usable during the press step, since vampires going to torpor do
not reach the press step).

Tom Wylie later (1 October 1995) used (or rather, explained) an
example of using PF when a Strike: Combat Ends resolves, "because
the round is now ending." - indicating his belief the PF was to be
played at the end of a round.

An update, of sorts, on the timing matter came from Tom Wylie on 25
February 1996:

Pulled Fangs is played when the round ends, regardless of when the
round ends. For example, if you send a vampire to torpor via
aggravated damage, you can yank its Fangs on its way out, even though
you haven't reached the press step yet.

When someone questioned as a departure from the "during press step"
ruling, Tom Wylie replied "This [the new statement, quoted above]
was simply was a mistake on my part (I had Taste of Vitae on the

backing out, but you can't force someone to block in the first place.

LSJ (vte...@wizards.com) wrote:

: Joshua Duffin wrote:
: > Currently, combat ends when a combatant is no longer ready (is burned
: > or goes to torpor), or when a Strike:Combat Ends resolves, or if there
: > are no presses to continue at the end of a round. With any of these

: > way to 'combat ends', and only after 'round ends' is over do you
: > actually leave 'combat'.

: I'd word it that the round ends when the combat ends, but OK.

My take on this derived from the Rules Outline details on how to handle
combat. It's divided into sections A-H; G is Round Ends, and H is Combat
Ends. That division led me to the idea that 'round ends' is essentially
a time period in the same way that 'establish range' or 'as combat is
entered' are time periods.

Of course, the Rules Outline may not be a definitive document, but it's
the best thing we've had, I think. ;-) Although I just noticed what looks
like an error in the combat section: in E.2.d, it says to go to step
F if one or both combatants are no longer ready, but step F is Presses -
I think that should probably say to go to G, 'Round Ends'.

: > During the end-of-round phase, you can
: > play Pulled Fangs;

: Unless some special effect is ending combat (like Rotschreck, Strike:
: Combat Ends, etc.). Such effects' resolutions cannot be interrupted,
: and once the effect is resolved, combat is over. Combat cards (like
: Pulled Fangs) cannot be played after combat.

If Strike:Combat Ends does this, the Rules Outline may need to be changed
to reflect that. It says at E.2.a.i, under Resolving Strikes, that when
a Strike:Combat Ends resolves, you go to step G (Round Ends) and that
any damage done by the strike is applied after combat (after step H).

I agree that Rotschreck may end combat 'instantaneously'; Elysium probably
does the same thing. But I would like it, for consistency's sake,
if all combats ended the same way.

Also, for Strike:Combat Ends, Drawing out the Beast has historically
been able to inflict damage before the combat is actually over - but
it can only do that if it 'knows' that the round is ending. I don't
know if there's ever been a ruling on whether DotB damage occurs vs
Rotschreck.

: There's no special "end of round" phase: Pulled Fangs can at the end

: of a round (during the press step, after all presses) and can be
: played if the round is ending prematurely (with the opposing vampire
: going to torpor, for instance).

Looking at the updated rulebook, it appears that the intent was to
simplify things in some respects, and combat is now described as having
three steps in each round: Determine Range, Strike, and Press. But
that still doesn't seem to include everything: before-range effects
have to be played 'before the acting minion decides whether or not
to play a maneuver at the start of this phase'. So I would say we
might as well keep the 'end of round' phase from the Rules Outline,
unless there's some compelling reason to get rid of it.

(aside on the new rulebook: It is on the whole very good. But I want
to pick some nits on the Strike:Combat Ends description. It does say
above it, in the Strikes section, that opposing strikes are resolved
simultaneously. But the wording 'This type of strike is
always the first to resolve, even before a strike done with First Strike,
and ends combat before other strikes can be resolved or any damage dealt'
could be taken to imply that an acting minion's S:CE ends combat before
the opposing minion's S:CE resolves - it might be good to clarify that,
although it's possible that this is something only those used to the
old descriptions would even think of. And the 'or any damage dealt'
part might want to note that this only means damage from strikes (or
other damage dealt at the same time as strikes or later); it won't
avoid Weather Control or Drawing out the Beast damage.)

Josh

Messages.Author: Joshua Duffin
Messages.Body:
agen...@my-dejanews.com wrote:

: > > Which, by the way is impossible now, as the first point of aggravated
: > > does no damage.

: > It does one damage. And it cannot be healed.

: Ok, this is bugging me. Everytime I think I have a handle on how
: the new agg damage works, I read something that has me wondering all
: over again.

: Situation:

: Vamp A 5/5 in combat with Vamp B 2/2
: Vamp A does 2 Aggro damage to Vamp B

: Does Vamp B drop into Torpor with 0 blood? Or 1 blood?

1 blood. The difference being pointed out above is that the first point
of agg damage *does* count as damage (so it's not 'no damage').

Under the current rules, any time a vampire takes damage, it has to
either burn blood to heal that damage or else go to torpor. Aggravated
damage can never be healed. So if a vampire takes one point of agg
damage and nothing else, it burns no blood (because it can't be healed),
but must go to torpor. (Because it has unhealed damage.) If
a vampire is already going to torpor (is 'wounded') and takes further
agg damage, it must burn a blood for each agg to avoid beind burned.

So if Bear Paw smacks Lupo with a Lucky Blow+Wolf Claws, Lupo has 2
agg damage on him. When we go to damage resolution, Lupo neglects to
prevent any of it during damage prevention. So we go to heal/etc.
The first point of agg cannot be healed, so Lupo is now wounded. The
second point sees that Lupo is already wounded, so he must burn a
blood to avoid being burned. He has one, so he burns it. That's all
the damage, so Lupo goes to torpor with 1 blood on him.

If instead we had Bear Paw with 3 Wolf Companions, and Bear Paw hit
Lupo with a 1-damage hand strike plus Wolf Claws, Lupo would be taking
3 normal and 1 aggravated damage. Lupo would burn 1 blood to heal the
first point of normal damage. He would burn 1 blood to heal the second
point of normal damage. He would become wounded by the third point of
normal damage. The single point of agg damage forces Lupo to burn a
blood or be destroyed, since he is already wounded. As he has no blood,
poor Lupo is burned.

This last scenario is where the current system differs most obviously
from the old Jyhad system. The old Jyhad system operated under a
'packeting' concept, which essentially meant that agg damage never burned
vampires unless there were at least 2 points of agg from a single
source of damage. That is no longer the case.

It differs from the more recent VTES rules in that, under those rules,
every point of agg damage required the recipient to burn a blood to
avoid destruction. That is no longer the case. Now the recipient must
only burn a blood to avoid destruction if he is already wounded.

(It has always been the case that, when resolving damage, normal damage
is handled first - ie the recipient burns blood to heal normal damage
before it starts burning blood to prevent destruction from agg damage.
This is still the case.)

Josh
